features.heading: Why Use WatermarkGemini to Remove Unwanted Objects?
features.intro: A targeted mask gives you control over which part of the photo changes, so the rest of the scene can stay useful.

items.heading: Precisely Mark Objects with Brush and Lasso
items.description: You decide which part of the image needs cleanup. Use the brush for irregular edges or a freehand lasso for a compact object, then inspect the blue mask before processing. This is better suited to selective object removal than an automatic background remover, because the subject and the rest of the scene should stay in place. Refine the selection with Eraser or Undo to avoid repainting details you want to keep.
items.imageAlt: Illustrative before view of a bicycle leaning against a stone wall.
items.afterImageAlt: Illustrative after view of the stone wall after the bicycle is removed from the scene.

items.heading: Remove People and Clutter from Your Photos
items.description: Travel photos, room shots, and social images often contain one person, sign, bag, or piece of clutter that distracts from the main subject. WatermarkGemini lets you select those elements individually rather than applying a broad edit to the whole image. Cover the object and any relevant shadow so the AI has the best chance to blend the replacement into the surrounding textures.
items.imageAlt: Illustrative before view of a portrait with a person walking behind the subject.
items.afterImageAlt: Illustrative after view of the same portrait with the background passerby absent.

items.heading: Rebuild the Background Behind the Object
items.description: AI inpainting estimates a replacement using nearby colors, texture, lighting, and structure. It can be effective for a small mark against a repeatable surface, but complex patterns or large objects may need several passes or may not reconstruct the exact hidden scene. Preview straight lines, repeating bricks, reflections, and people’s outlines carefully before using the final photo.
items.imageAlt: Illustrative before view of a flowering plant standing against a brick wall.
items.afterImageAlt: Illustrative after view of the same brick wall without the flowering plant.

faq.heading: Remove Object from Image FAQs
faq.intro: Answers to the most common questions about use cases, formats, results, pricing, and safe editing.

items.question: How do I remove an object from an image online?
items.answer: Upload the photo, use the brush or lasso to mark the object you want removed, and check that the entire item and its shadow are selected. Apply the AI cleanup, compare the result with your original, and download the PNG when the background looks natural.

items.question: Can I remove an object from an image for free?
items.answer: Eligible accounts may receive limited free image uses. The available allowance and any processing cost are shown in the workspace; free access is not an unlimited editing guarantee.

items.question: Can AI remove an unwanted person from a photo?
items.answer: You can mark an incidental person in a photo you are entitled to edit and ask the tool to rebuild the area behind them. Results depend on how much of the scene was hidden and whether nearby frames or pixels provide consistent context.

items.question: Should I use the brush or lasso tool?
items.answer: Choose the brush for narrow or irregular shapes, such as cables and hands. Choose the lasso for a compact item, then refine the mask with Eraser or Undo. Either way, include the full shadow if it is part of the distraction.

items.question: Will object removal blur the background?
items.answer: AI fills the selected area by estimating the background. Fine textures, faces, and architectural lines may still show artifacts. Zoom in and examine the result rather than assuming the hidden pixels have been exactly restored.

items.question: Can I remove objects without removing the background?
items.answer: Yes. This workflow is for targeting one distraction within the photo while keeping the remaining scene. For cutting out an entire subject onto transparency, use the separate Background Remover.

items.question: Can I remove text or logos with this object remover?
items.answer: Small incidental text or logos in your own pictures may be selected for cleanup, but specialized Remove Text and Remove Logo pages better explain those scenarios. Only remove marks you are permitted to edit.

items.question: Which image formats can I upload?
items.answer: The current page supports common image formats, with a displayed file limit of 10 MB, and describes PNG download. Check the live uploader for the final accepted input list before publishing exact format claims.

items.question: How do I remove a shadow with an object?
items.answer: Cover the object and the cast shadow in the same selection when they form one visual distraction. A tight mask that excludes the shadow may leave a noticeable trace even after the object disappears.

items.question: Can I remove multiple objects in one photo?
items.answer: You may select more than one unwanted area, but complex multi-object edits can produce inconsistent fills. For better control, start with the most prominent object, review the result, and make additional passes if your workflow allows.

items.question: Does removing an object change the photo’s original quality?
items.answer: The edited region is newly inferred content, not the recovered original scene. Other pixels and export encoding may also differ depending on the tool. Keep the source photo and review important details before publishing or printing.
